verses.text: Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel had gone there to make him king.
Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard about it. He was still in Egypt, where he had run away from King Solomon, and he was living there.
The people sent for him, and Jeroboam and the whole assembly of Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam. They said,
"Your father put a heavy load on us. Now make the hard work and the heavy load your father put on us lighter, and we will serve you."
Rehoboam answered, "Go away for three days, then come back to me." So the people left.
King Rehoboam asked advice from the older men who had served his father Solomon while he was alive. He asked, "What do you advise me to answer these people?"
They said, "If today you will be a servant to these people and serve them, and give them a kind answer, they will be your servants forever."
But Rehoboam rejected the advice the older men gave him. He asked advice from the young men who had grown up with him and now served him.
He asked them, "What do you advise? How should we answer these people who told me, 'Make the load your father put on us lighter'?"

The young men who had grown up with him said, "These people told you, 'Your father made our load heavy, but make it lighter for us.' Tell them this: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.
My father put a heavy load on you, but I will make it even heavier. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions.'"
On the third day, Jeroboam and all the people came back to Rehoboam, just as the king had told them: "Come back to me on the third day."
The king answered the people harshly. He rejected the advice the older men had given him.
He followed the advice of the young men and said, "My father made your load heavy, but I will make it even heavier. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions."
So the king did not listen to the people. This was from the LORD, so that what the LORD had said through Ahijah from Shiloh to Jeroboam the son of Nebat would come true.

When all Israel saw that the king would not listen to them, they answered him, "What share do we have in David? We have no part in the son of Jesse! Go home to your tents, Israel! David, look after your own house now!" So the Israelites went home.
But Rehoboam still ruled over the Israelites who lived in the towns of Judah.
Then King Rehoboam sent out Adoram, who was in charge of the forced workers, but all Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam quickly climbed into his chariot and escaped to Jerusalem.
So Israel has rebelled against David's family to this day.
When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had come back, they called him to a meeting and made him king over all Israel. No one stayed loyal to David's family except the tribe of Judah.

When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he gathered all the people of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, one hundred and eighty thousand chosen soldiers. They were going to fight against Israel and win the kingdom back for Rehoboam the son of Solomon.
But God's word came to Shemaiah the man of God. God said,
"Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the people of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people. Tell them,

'The LORD says: Do not go up and fight against your relatives, the people of Israel. Every one of you, go home, because I have made this happen.'" So they obeyed the LORD's word and went home, just as the LORD had said.
Then Jeroboam built up Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. From there he went out and built up Penuel.
Jeroboam thought to himself, "Now the kingdom might go back to David's family.

If these people go up to offer sacrifices at the LORD's temple in Jerusalem, their hearts will turn back to their master, Rehoboam king of Judah. Then they will kill me and go back to Rehoboam king of Judah."
So after getting advice, the king made two gold calves. He told the people, "It is too much trouble for you to go up to Jerusalem. Look, Israel, here are your gods who brought you up out of Egypt!"
He put one calf in Bethel and the other in Dan.
This became a sin, because the people went as far as Dan to worship the calf there.
Jeroboam built shrines on high places and chose priests from all kinds of people, even though they were not from the tribe of Levi.

Jeroboam started a festival on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the festival in Judah, and he offered sacrifices on the altar. He did this in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves he had made. He also placed in Bethel the priests of the high places he had made.

On the fifteenth day of the eighth month, a month he had chosen on his own, he went up to the altar he had made in Bethel. He started a festival for the Israelites and went up to the altar to burn incense.
